# Customer Due Diligence (CDD) & Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) — Jersey MLO Summary

## Standard CDD (core requirements)
- Identify the customer and verify identity using reliable, independent source documents/data
- Identify and verify beneficial owners / controllers (understand ownership and control structure)
- Obtain information on the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship
- Conduct ongoing monitoring of the relationship and transactions

## Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) — when required
- Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) — foreign and domestic (and family/close associates)
- Customers from or connected to high-risk jurisdictions
- Complex or unusually large transactions, or unusual patterns with no apparent economic or lawful purpose
- Correspondent relationships
- Private banking / higher risk products
- When the customer is not physically present
- When there is higher risk indicated by the business or customer risk assessment

EDD measures typically include:
- Senior management approval for the relationship
- Enhanced source of funds / source of wealth information and verification
- Enhanced ongoing monitoring
- Additional information on the purpose of the relationship

## Simplified Due Diligence
Only permitted in clearly low-risk situations as defined by the Order and Handbook. Never automatic.

## Beneficial Ownership
- Understand and verify the ownership and control structure
- Identify the ultimate beneficial owner(s) (typically >25% or significant control)
- For trusts and other vehicles, identify settlors, trustees, protectors, beneficiaries, etc.

## Record Keeping
- CDD records, risk assessments, transaction records, training records
- Generally retain for at least 5 years after the end of the business relationship or occasional transaction

## Source of Funds / Wealth
Increasingly important, especially in EDD and higher-risk relationships. Document and verify where risk requires.

Cross-reference with the latest JFSC Handbook for sector-specific detail.
